passage: Fenwick Community Pool, lane swimming, winter schedule. Lane reservations cannot be made on our website this winter while the online system is replaced. prompt: [Daily Life — notice] A swimmer comes to the 6 a.m. lane hour without having contacted the pool. According to the notice, what happens?

The swimmer is turned away and asked to come back later that morning.
The swimmer can swim, because that hour takes no reservation.
The swimmer can swim only if someone with a reservation fails to arrive.
correct_answer: The swimmer can swim, because that hour takes no reservation.
explanation: The notice states that the 6 a.m. lane hour takes no reservation at all and that swimmers should just show up and wait in line.

distractor_rationales.choice: The swimmer waits ten minutes before any lane can be used.
distractor_rationales.reason: Borrows the ten-minute rule, which governs a reserved lane whose holder is late, not an unreserved arrival.

distractor_rationales.choice: The swimmer is turned away and asked to come back later that morning.
distractor_rationales.reason: The natural assumption if every lane needed holding, which the notice rules out for the 6 a.m. hour.

distractor_rationales.choice: The swimmer can swim only if someone with a reservation fails to arrive.
distractor_rationales.reason: True of the released-lane rule elsewhere in the notice, but not of the 6 a.m. hour.
